title: Choose ClearCam’s operating world
question: ClearCam is a private camera hub on one person’s Mac. Choose the visual world for its local command surface.

options.label: The household observatory
options.lineage: a quiet home observatory and a well-kept field notebook
options.thesis: The home is being calmly observed, not theatrically surveilled.
options.viewport: A single generous live view anchors the left; today’s observed moments form a precise timeline to the right; one calm action opens camera setup.
options.risk: Requires restrained detail so it stays useful rather than becoming atmospheric.

options.label: Signal bench
options.lineage: a CRT oscilloscope and test bench
options.thesis: Every camera becomes a signal that can be armed, inspected, and made reliable.
options.viewport: Live video shares a measured graticule with health traces and a small set of detented control actions.
options.risk: Strong for reliability, but risks making home monitoring feel like lab equipment.
options.case: Strong audience identification for a technical owner, but weaker product clarity for reviewing real-world events.

options.label: Graphite instrument desk
options.thesis: Camera state is clear at a glance, with every risky control deliberately separated.
options.viewport: A persistent tiled workspace foregrounds camera health, with event review and controls in stable panels.
options.risk: Very usable, but less memorable and more likely to resemble a generic technical dashboard.
options.case: Excellent clarity, but loses on audience identification because it treats a private home like enterprise infrastructure.

options.label: Living glyph scene
options.lineage: a live scene rendered in text characters
options.thesis: The camera feed becomes a tactile, low-bandwidth field of moving light.
options.viewport: A live character-field introduces the feed, with practical event controls held in a clear lower rail.
options.risk: Memorable, but fuses poorly with trustworthy event review and accessible imagery.
options.case: It wins novelty but loses both product clarity and practical use, so it is not recommended.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A familiar camera dashboard, executed cleanly and without a distinctive operating world.
canonCard.viewport: A standard header, grid of camera cards, and events table below.
canonCard.risk: Fast to recognize but forgettable, and it does not express ClearCam’s privacy-first point of view.
